themes_detail.label: Dead trees spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 4 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike versus the 0.5 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.0)—signaling either acute tree die-off or a sudden reporting surge, potentially linked to drought, disease, or pest damage requiring urgent forestry intervention.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
700% spike with z-score of 7.0 (statistically significant high-severity anomaly)
Chronic budget request: Forestry services & street tree maintenance (repeated year over year)
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden spike in dead tree reports—disease, drought, pests, or contractor negligence?
Interview Parks Department on timeline for tree removal and whether staffing/budget constraints are delaying response

themes_detail.label: Public drinking complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Drinking-related 311 complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike from the 0.5 weekly average—indicating a potential new or intensifying public intoxication issue in a historically high-traffic tourist and residential district.
evidence: 4 drinking complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
700% spike with z-score of 7.0 (same magnitude as dead tree spike)
Encampment complaints consistently high (485 over 90 days), suggesting possible convergence with substance use issues
reporting_angles: Is public drinking concentrated in specific parks or blocks? Interview NYPD and community residents.
Are bars, restaurants, or venues over-serving alcohol, or is this driven by unhoused populations? Investigate licensing complaints.

themes_detail.label: Construction complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints spiked to 34 THIS WEEK—a 169% increase versus the 12.6 weekly average—amid 1,738 active DOB permit filings (1,503 alteration permits), suggesting disruptive renovation activity or code violations tied to the district's ongoing building activity.
evidence: 34 construction/plumbing complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.6 weekly baseline (8-week average), 169% spike with z-score 5.01
1,738 total DOB permit filings in 90 days, dominated by 1,503 alteration permits
Chronic budget request: housing inspections & code violation correction (repeated annual request indicates ongoing enforcement gap)
reporting_angles: Are alteration permits being issued without adequate oversight? Interview DOB about complaint-to-violation conversion rates.
Which buildings generate the most complaints? Map complaints against permit clusters to identify problem contractors or properties.

themes_detail.label: Dead animal complaints spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints jumped to 4 LAST WEEK—a 433% spike from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.51)—suggesting either a pest infestation, rodent die-off, or public health hazard requiring rapid sanitation response.
evidence: 4 dead animal complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (8-week average), 433% spike with z-score 7.51
Chronic budget request: increased sanitation trucks & equipment (suggests strain on waste response capacity)
reporting_angles: Interview Sanitation Department and Health Department on response times and cleanup protocols.
Is this indicative of a broader pest control problem in the district? Cross-reference with rat complaint patterns.

themes_detail.label: Consumer complaints rising
themes_detail.summary: Consumer complaints nearly doubled to 19 THIS WEEK—a 141% spike from the 7.9 weekly average (z-score: 5.86)—indicating either merchant fraud, food safety, or vendor misconduct concentrated in Greenwich Village/SoHo's dense commercial corridor.
evidence: 19 consumer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.9 weekly baseline (8-week average), 141% spike with z-score 5.86
Mobile food vendor complaints also up 367% (7 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 avg), suggesting street vendor misconduct cluster
Vendor enforcement consistently high in baseline (369 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: What types of consumer complaints are dominating—food safety, fraud, short-changing? FOIA DOE data.
Are mobile food vendors the common thread? Interview Health Department on inspection frequency and enforcement.
